result.title: AvoKV-E: Payload-Aware KV Cache Eviction for Long Reasoning
result.summary: Long-output reasoning shifts the KV-cache bottleneck from the fixed prompt to the generated trace. Existing reasoning-cache eviction methods largely treat cached entries as routing objects, estimating whether an old key will still be read, will recur, or can be replaced. This routing-only view overlooks two effects: low-attention entries can carry large value payloads whose removal changes future predictions, and newly generated states can appear stale before later queries have had a chance to read them. We introduce AvoKV-E, a training-free eviction policy that first delays eligibility for recent states and then ranks eligible entries using candidate-normalized read pressure, key redundancy, and value-payload potential. According to empirical evaluation across different models and datasets, AvoKV-E matches or exceeds redundancy-aware, recurrence-based, and thought-adaptive eviction baselines at matched active-KV budgets, with its largest gains in the tightest-cache regime. Component and counterfactual analyses further connect these gains to delayed observation, payload-aware scoring, redundancy, and scale-robust normalization. Together, the results show that long-reasoning KV eviction should preserve not only keys that are likely to be read, but also the value payloads that sustain the reasoning trajectory.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 AvoKV-E，一种无需训练的 KV 缓存逐出策略：先对刚生成的近期状态延迟其被逐出资格，再用候选归一化的读取压力、键冗余度和 value 载荷潜力对候选条目排序，以在长输出推理中维持固定活跃 KV 预算。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“读取—载荷”双视角与延迟观察的逐出判据，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态何时可丢弃、视觉证据保留多少的 STOP/缓存策略提供线索，尤其值得核查低注意力却高载荷的条目是否对应任务必要信息。
